The FOMC statement (Dec 19, 2018) is moderately positive with a mild hawkish tilt—citing strong labor markets, robust household spending, inflation near 2%, and a rate hike with guidance for “some further gradual increases.” However, the SLOOS points to tighter credit conditions and softer loan demand that temper this tone: banks tightened standards and other terms for C&I loans and for construction and land development lending, and reported weaker demand in construction/land development. These SLOOS findings align with the statement’s note that business fixed investment has moderated and suggest credit headwinds that could weigh on capex and construction. Combined with financial stability concerns around leveraged lending, the overall assessment leans more cautious than a pure macro read, implying a slower, more careful normalization path rather than aggressive tightening.
